From humble national beginnings in the 1990s and
a lengthy hiatus, the Bathurst 12 Hour Race, held
at Mount Panorama in Australia, had developed
into an international endurance classic since 2007.
In the early touring car era, BMW had already secured
two overall victories, but since 2011, when the pop-
ular GT3 cars began to dominate, the Munich-based
manufacturer had long been chasing a win without
success. The rollercoaster circuit around Mount
Panorama, east of Sydney, seemed to be cursed for
BMW. In 2025, the WRT BMW Team therefore en-
tered two BMW M4 GT3s with top-class line-ups for
the endurance race.
The spell
— ee
‘broken
The #46 car was shared by Valentino Rossi, Raffaele
Marciello and Charles Weerts, whilst the #32 M4
GT3 was shared by brothers Kelvin and Sheldon van
der Linde alongside veteran Augusto Farfus. Although
the two BMWs were not quite at the front of the grid
in qualifying, WRT made the most of the M4 GT3’s
superior range. It was the last time that the M4 raced
without the Evo package. WRT skilfully defended an
early one-two lead through strategic manoeuvres
and capitalised on the yellow flag periods. When
Rossi picked up a drive-through penalty shortly be-
fore the end, victory was secured for the van der
Linde brothers and Augusto Farfus. The Bathurst
spell had finally been broken.
